description: Data underlying the publication: A rainfall threshold-based approach to early warnings in urban data-scarce regions: A case study of pluvial flooding in Alexandria, Egypt is a hazard data set listed in DataCite country sweep of research-data repositories (Africa), a research data metadata index, published or maintained by 4TU.ResearchData. This study aims to utilise a probabilistic approach to characterise and predict urban floods by assessing critical rainfall thresholds likely to cause flooding combined with ensemble precipitation forecast in Alexandria, Egypt. Rainfall thresholds were inferred by associating observed rainfall and historical flood information sourced from social media and newspapers. Coverage: Egypt. The portal files it under the publisher 4TU.ResearchData. Its tags are Atmospheric Sciences, FOS: Earth and related environmental sciences, Earth Sciences, pluvial flood forecasting, early warning systems. The repository dates the deposit 2025; no later update was checked. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support hazard exposure and risk screening for infrastructure. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-africa-dc-portal.
